name: Whites Marrying Blacks
overview: Scripture shows that distinctions of ethnicity and social status are ultimately transcended in Christ, as believers are united beyond national, cultural, and social divisions (Galatians 3:28; Colossians 3:11). The example of Moses marrying an Ethiopian woman (Numbers 12:1) illustrates that interracial marriage was present in biblical times and not condemned. God created all nations from one blood, establishing their boundaries and times (Acts 17:26), emphasizing the unity and equality of all people. Believers are called to judge righteously rather than by outward appearances (John 7:24), affirming that in Christ, such distinctions should not hinder relationships, including marriage.
